prompt_text: I need a dental implant in Phoenix. Which specific dental practices should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Phoenix for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
I can do that — I just need one quick detail: do you want providers inside Phoenix proper or the greater Phoenix metro (Tempe, Scottsdale, Mesa, Glendale)? Also do you prefer a specialist (periodontist or oral/maxillofacial surgeon or prosthodontist) or are you okay with a general dentist who places implants?

If you want, I can then give a short list of specific practices to call plus why to call each one. If you’d rather get started right away, here are immediate, practical steps and exactly what to ask when you call.

If you want a list of specific practices, tell me which area (ZIP or neighborhood) and your specialist preference and I’ll tailor recommendations.

If you want to start calling right away, use this plan and script

1) Which types of practices to call (call several of each)
- Periodontists — specialists in gums and implant placement for complex bone/gum issues.
- Oral & maxillofacial surgeons — good for extractions, bone grafts, complicated anatomy, IV sedation.
- Prosthodontists — specialists in the restorative/crown part of the implant (important for complex restorations or full-arch work).
- Implant-focused general dentists — often fine for straightforward single-tooth implants and coordinate with specialists when needed.

2) Where to find reputable local providers
- AAID (American Academy of Implant Dentistry) “Find a Dentist”
- American Academy of Periodontology “Find a Specialist”
- American Association of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons “Find a Surgeon”
- Zocdoc, Healthgrades, Google Maps / Yelp (look for many recent 4+ star reviews)
- Your dental insurance directory (if cost/coverage matters)

3) Phone/script — exact questions to ask (say this on the phone)
“Hi, I’m considering a dental implant for [single tooth / multiple / full-arch]. Do you do implant placement/restorations in-house? What specialist will handle placement and who will make the crown? Will you do a CBCT (3D) scan and virtual planning? How many implants do you place per year? Do you offer IV sedation or oral sedation? Do you handle bone grafting/sinus lifts if needed? What brand(s) of implants do you use? What’s the cost range for placement plus restoration (and what’s included)? Is there a written warranty or follow-up policy? Do you accept my insurance/offer financing? Can I see before-and-after photos and patient references?”

4) What to prioritize when comparing practices
- Volume & experience: clinics that place many implants tend to have better outcomes.
- Specialist skill mix: team that includes surgeon + prosthodontist is ideal for complex cases.
- Use of CBCT 3D imaging and digital treatment planning/guided surgery.
- Clear pricing and staged estimates (extraction, grafting, implant, abutment, crown).
- Implant brand and warranty information (Nobel Biocare, Straumann, Zimmer, etc., are widely used reputable systems).
- Patient reviews and before/after photos.
- Comfort options (sedation) and pain/aftercare protocols.
- Good communication and follow-up: who you call if a problem arises.

5) Logistics to confirm during/after an initial consult
- Request digital CBCT and treatment plan with timeline.
- Ask for a full written estimate and payment options.
- Confirm who will restore the implant (same office or a separate provider) and see a sample of their crown work.
- Ask about possible complications and how they are handled.

If you tell me your ZIP code/neighborhood and whether you prefer a specialist or general dentist, I’ll give a tailored list of 5–8 specific Phoenix-area practices to call and a one-line reason for each (e.g., “periodontist with 20+ years implant experience,” “oral surgeon offering same-day implants and IV sedation,” “prosthodontist specializing in full-arch restorations”). I can also draft a short text or email you can send to offices if you prefer not to call.
